misconceptions.description: Writing generic worries in the equity column instead of context-specific risks tied to real student groups
misconceptions.trigger: candidate lists risks that could apply to any school and any tool
misconceptions.feedback: Name a real subgroup in this placement and the mechanism by which the tool could disadvantage them.

misconceptions.description: Recording a vendor's bias-tested claim as settled equity evidence
misconceptions.trigger: candidate enters a marketing fairness claim without asking who was tested
misconceptions.feedback: Log vendor fairness claims as unverified. Ask which groups were tested, on what data, and whether your students were represented.

misconceptions.description: Pasting AI-generated generic risks into the matrix as if they were the context audit
misconceptions.trigger: candidate fills the equity column with risks that mention no specific student group or policy
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI risks as prompts, then ground each one in this placement's actual students, devices, and policies.

misconceptions.description: Treating a fully completed matrix as proof of a defensible equity recommendation
misconceptions.trigger: candidate offers a filled grid, price, or preference instead of risk, safeguard, and monitoring
misconceptions.feedback: Pair each risk with the affected group, the safeguard, and a post-rollout check. A filled grid is not the analysis.
